capabilityIndex.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
capabilityIndex.attribution: Capability scores are published by Artificial Analysis and reproduced with attribution.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.note: OpenAI's frontier model, released 3 September 2026. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens use the standard long-context column on the pricing page: $20 input / $2 cached / $75 output for the whole request. The model documentation limits input to 922,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.note: OpenAI labels the published $4 input / $0.40 cached / $20 output rate as promotional pricing available until November 30, 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing). The pricing page does not state a separate post-promotion standard rate, so that published rate stays the headline. Prompts above 272K input tokens use the pricing table's long-context column, $8 input / $0.80 cached / $30 output, for the whole request. Maximum output is 128K tokens. No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row. The model documentation limits input to 922,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.note: Published short-context rates are $2 input / $0.20 cached / $12 output per 1M tokens. For prompts above 272K input tokens, the pricing table publishes $4 input / $0.40 cached / $18 output for the whole request. Maximum input is 922,000 tokens and maximum output is 128,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.note: Published short-context rates are $0.20 input / $0.02 cached / $1.20 output per 1M tokens. For prompts above 272K input tokens, the pricing table publishes $0.40 input / $0.04 cached / $1.80 output for the whole request. Maximum input is 922,000 tokens and maximum output is 128,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.note: Frontier reasoning and agentic model; succeeds Opus 4.8.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.note: Cache hits and refreshes are priced at 0.025x base input ($0.25 / 1M) instead of the usual 0.1x. Supersedes Claude Fable 5.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.note: Permanent standard rate ($2 input / $10 output / $0.20 cached). No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.note: Prices unchanged at $1 input / $0.10 cache read / $5 output. The Sonnet 5.5 model comparison lists a 200K context window and 64K maximum output (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview). The models overview lists Claude Haiku 4.5 among Legacy models that remain available (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview). The deprecations table lists claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 as Active, with retirement not sooner than October 15, 2026 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations). No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.note: Standard price shown for prompts up to 200K tokens (inclusive). Prompts above 200K bill $4 input, $0.40 cached input, and $18 output per million tokens. No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.note: Standard rate shown. An introductory rate of $0.75 input / $0.075 cached / $3.75 output runs through December 31, 2026. 1M input limit with 64K max output.

models.name: Grok 4.6
models.note: Prompts at or above 200K use $4 input, $1 cached input, and $12 output per million tokens.

models.name: Grok 4.5
models.note: Prompts at or above 200K use $4 input, $0.60 cached input, and $12 output per million tokens. No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row.

models.name: Grok Build 0.1
models.note: The official release notes confirm grok-build-0.1 reached end of life on November 19, 2026 and is no longer served on the xAI API. The former model URL redirects to the current model list. The last published rates and 500K context are retained for historical comparisons, including $2 input / $0.40 cached / $4 output per 1M above the 200K input threshold. Grok 4.7 is the catalog replacement with its own prices; no automatic provider redirect is asserted. OpenCode still advertises this ID in its public model list (https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/models), but that conflicts with the upstream retirement notice and is not treated as verified current access.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.note: DeepSeek lists the current endpoint as V4 Pro 0813. Headline input and output use the published peak rates. Off-peak input and output are $0.66 and $1.98 per 1M tokens. Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC on weekdays, excluding Chinese public holidays. The displayed $0.0266 cache rate approximates a non-holiday week using 35 hours at $0.044 and 133 at $0.022.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.note: Deprecated on 10/31/2026 and scheduled to retire on 4/30/2027. The models overview lists API id mistral-large-2512 and names Mistral Large 4 as the alternative (https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/models/). The inference pricing page no longer lists this model, so the stored rates are the last published ones. No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row.

models.name: Codestral
models.note: Codestral v25.08 (codestral-latest) publishes a 128K context window and $0.30 input / $0.90 output per 1M tokens. The current pricing table does not print a separate cached-input rate. The stored $0.03 rate is derived as 10% of $0.30 under the official prompt-caching billing rule, for tokens reported as cache hits (https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching). No Intelligence Index score has been verified for this row.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.note: Flagship 1M context model; available through GLM Coding Plan and OpenCode Zen.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.note: Standard rate shown; the 50% promotional rate that ran through September 9, 2026 has ended. Cached input storage is free for a limited time.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.note: Also available through OpenCode Zen; web search is billed separately. Only the low-effort variant has a published v5.0.2 score in this pass; the max-effort score is unpublished. This row records low effort and does not estimate max effort.

models.name: Kimi K2.7 Code
models.note: Coding-specialized API; not ranked for general writing or research. Kimi's pricing page says K2 series models are closed to newly registered users from October 31, 2026, and all K2 series models are planned to retire by the end of December 2026 (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat). Existing users are unaffected until then. The row stays because OpenCode Go, Go Plus, and Zen still list it. No Intelligence Index v5.0.2 score has been verified for this row.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
models.note: Standard tier, not used to improve Meta products. A contributor tier (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) costs $0.10 input / $0.002 cached / $0.20 output in exchange for allowing Meta to train on prompts and outputs.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Max
models.note: International (Singapore) endpoint rate. The Beijing, US, Germany, Japan, and Hong Kong endpoints bill lower at $1.65 input / $0.206 cached / $4.951 output. Max input is 991,808 tokens of the 1M window.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
models.note: DeepSeek identifies the current deepseek-flash endpoint as V4.1 Flash 1017; the retired V4 Flash aliases route to it. Headline input and output use the published peak rates. Off-peak input and output are $0.15 and $0.60 per 1M tokens. Peak hours are 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC on weekdays, excluding Chinese public holidays. The displayed $0.0036 cache rate approximates a non-holiday week using 35 hours at $0.006 and 133 at $0.003. The Intelligence Index score uses the 1017 snapshot at max effort.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.note: Released 21 September 2026 at Grok 4.6 prices. Prompts at or above 200K use $4 input, $1 cached input, and $12 output per million tokens. A fast variant, available through Cursor and Grok Build only, uses 2x standard token rates, or 1.5x the long-context rates (https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing).

models.name: Step 5 Preview
models.note: StepFun's flagship agentic model, released 18 September 2026. Sparse mixture-of-experts with text, image and video input. Re-read October 19, 2026 from the pricing page: $1 input, $0.10 cache hit, and $2.70 output per million tokens. Maximum output is 64K tokens, and output tokens include the reasoning trace. The cache-miss input price covers writing new content to the cache.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.note: Succeeds Opus 5 at a lower price. Cache reads are 0.05x input rather than Anthropic's usual 0.1x. The full 1M window is billed at standard rates; fast mode ($8 / $40) is a separate premium tier, not the headline rate.

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.note: GPT-6 mid tier, built for complex coding and agentic work. Half the published GPT-5.6 Sol price. Maximum output is 128K tokens. The model page states that prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the whole request. The long-context band ($4 input / $0.40 cached / $15 output) is derived from that multiplier applied to the published $2 / $0.20 / $10 rates. The current pricing table also publishes these long-context rates. The model documentation limits input to 922,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.note: OpenAI's most efficient GPT-6 model, for focused, high-volume tasks. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens use the standard long-context column: $0.20 input / $0.02 cached / $0.75 output for the whole request. The model documentation limits input to 922,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.note: Newer Sol model, described by OpenAI as near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost. Same input and output rates as GPT-6 Sol with half the cached rate. GPT-6 Sol remains available. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens use the standard long-context column: $4 input / $0.20 cached / $15 output for the whole request. The model documentation limits input to 922,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.note: Released September 28, 2026. Cache reads were cut from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens on October 7, 2026 (0.05x base input). 5-minute cache writes stay $2.50 and 1-hour cache writes stay $4. The Batch API is 50% off input and output. US-only inference is 1.1x. Retirement is not sooner than September 28, 2027. Maximum output is 128K tokens on the synchronous API.

models.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
models.note: Released October 7, 2026. Prompts up to 100,000 tokens are $0.10 input / $0.01 cache read / $0.50 output; prompts over 100,000 tokens are $0.50 / $0.05 / $2.50 for the whole request. 5-minute cache writes are $0.125 below that line and $0.625 above it; 1-hour cache writes are $0.20 and $1. The Batch API is 50% off input and output. Synchronous maximum output is 128K tokens; the Message Batches API allows 300K with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header. Retirement is not sooner than October 7, 2027.

models.name: Mistral Large 4
models.note: Public Preview since October 6, 2026. Open-weight Mixture-of-Experts under the Mistral Ecosystem Open Weight License. The model card and the inference pricing table show $0.70 input / $0.07 cached input / $2.10 output per 1M tokens, with no sale wording (https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0, https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/pricing).

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.note: GA October 13, 2026. Standard rate from December 1, 2026 shown. An introductory rate of $2 input / $0.10 cached / $10 output runs through November 30, 2026. Implicit caching only (explicit caching not supported). One published rate applies across the full context window. Batch and Flex are 50% of standard; Priority is 1.8×. Context window is 1,048,576 tokens. Default synchronous max output is 65,536; long decode / background execution raises the hard ceiling to 1,048,576, and maxOutputTokens records that ceiling at the catalog 1M context bound. Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing and https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-4-argon.

models.name: Muse Wonder
models.note: Announced October 12, 2026. API id `muse-wonder-1.0`. Standard mode only on Model API; Contributor mode is not available for Muse Wonder on Model API. One published rate applies across the full window. The models page states a 1,048,576-token context window, recorded as 1.048576M. Muse Wonder Full is available only with a Muse Code subscription and has no public API price, so it is not listed. Muse Code High Usage ($15), Power Usage ($50), and Maximum Usage ($200) include Muse Wonder; Everyday Usage is $5 and stays under the catalog floor (https://dev.meta.ai/help/subscriptions/what-is-a-muse-code-subscription). The separate Muse agent Power ($20) and Maximum ($100) plans name a weekly token allowance and do not name this model (https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/). Meta One plan pages describe consumer AI usage and do not name it (https://www.meta.com/meta-one-plans/).

models.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
models.note: GA October 19, 2026. API id `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`. Early anonymous serving was Space Bunny. Thinking depth is tunable through effort (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; default `max`). Multimodal: text, image, and video input. The model guide states a 1,000,000-token context window. Prompt-cache reads are $0.015 per million tokens.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
models.note: Released October 23, 2026. API id `kimi-k3.1-pro`. One published rate applies across the full window. The pricing page states a 1,048,576-token context window, recorded as 1.048576M. Kimi bills cache misses, cache writes, and cache hits as separate slices of the same input tokens. The default 5-minute cache write is $2 per million tokens, the same as input, and the caching guide says that write was already included in the input price, so the stored input and cached rates cover the default. The optional 1-hour cache write is $4 per million tokens (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/context-caching). The separate id `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` is not listed. Kimi K3 remains the previous-generation model. Quickstart default max completion tokens is 131,072 and can be set up to 1,048,576. Sources: https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat , https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart , and https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro .

models.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
models.note: Released October 26, 2026. Published short-context rate is $1 input / $0.05 cached / $5 output. The model page states that prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request. The long-context band ($2 input / $0.10 cached / $7.50 output) is derived from that multiplier applied to the published $1 / $0.05 / $5 rates. 30-minute cache writes are $1.25 per million tokens and 12-hour cache writes are $2.50. Maximum output is 128K tokens. GPT-5.6 Terra remains available. Sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-terra , https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing , and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog . The model documentation limits input to 922,000 tokens of the 1.05M combined window.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.note: Standard API rates after MiniMax’s stated permanent discount. Above 512K input tokens the full request uses $0.60 input / $0.12 cached input / $2.40 output per 1M tokens.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.2
models.note: Released November 9, 2026. Standard global API rates apply across the full context window; cache reads cost 0.025× input. Fast mode costs $16 input / $80 output per 1M tokens and is not the headline rate. Sources: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing and https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-fable-5-2.

models.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
models.note: Generally available on the paid Gemini API since November 10, 2026. Headline rates are the standard rates from December 1, 2026; introductory rates are $2 input / $0.10 cached / $10 output per 1M tokens through November 30. Implicit caching only. The unified input/output context limit is 1,048,576 tokens; synchronous output defaults to 65,536, and long decode supports up to 1,048,576. Numeric limits use the same conservative 1M catalog bound as Argon. The high-effort score is from the current Intelligence Index v5.0.2 model page. Model details: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-carbon.

models.name: Muse Ember
models.note: API id muse-ember-1.0. Standard mode only on Model API; Contributor mode is not available there. For requests over 200K input tokens, cached tokens included, the entire request uses $0.30 input / $0.012 cached / $1.50 output per 1M tokens. Muse Ember is included in every Muse Code subscription. Model limits: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-ember. Benchmark: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/muse-ember.

models.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
models.note: Generally available since November 12, 2026. Standard paid-tier rates shown; the API also offers a free tier. Implicit caching only. The unified input/output context window is 1,048,576 tokens; synchronous output defaults to 65,536, and long decode supports up to 1,048,576. Numeric limits use the same conservative 1M catalog bound as Argon and Carbon. Thinking levels are low, medium, high (default), and xhigh. Sources: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-hydrogen, https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog#11-12-2026, and https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gemini-4-hydrogen.

models.name: GPT-6.2 Astra
models.note: Standard API rates. Input is limited to 922,000 tokens. Above 272K input tokens the full request costs $16 input / $0.80 cached / $60 output per 1M tokens.

models.name: GPT-6.2 Sol
models.note: Standard API rates. Input is limited to 922,000 tokens. Above 272K input tokens the full request costs $4 input / $0.20 cached / $15 output per 1M tokens.

models.name: Gemini 4 Neon
models.note: Generally available November 18, 2026 on the paid API. Implicit caching only. The unified input/output window is 1,048,576 tokens; synchronous output defaults to 65,536, and long decode supports the remaining unified window. Numeric limits use the same conservative 1M bound as the other Gemini 4 rows. Model limits: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-neon. Benchmark: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gemini-4-neon.

models.name: Qwen4-Max
models.note: Singapore International rates, in default thinking mode with a 983,616-token input ceiling and 262,144-token output ceiling. Cached reads cost $0.075 per 1M tokens on the official International console: https://modelstudio.console.alibabacloud.com/ap-southeast-1/model/market/detail/qwen4-max. Benchmark: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen4-max.

models.name: GLM-5.3-FlashX
models.note: Fast inference variant of GLM-5.3-Flash. The official model documentation confirms a 1M context window and 128K maximum output (https://docs.z.ai/guides/vlm/glm-5.3-flash). FlashX is not yet available on the GLM Coding Plan. Cached input storage is free for a limited time. No independently verified Intelligence Index score is available for this variant.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed
models.note: API ID kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed. The official pricing page publishes a 1,048,576-token context window and flat rates across it. Regular input and output cost twice standard K3.1 Pro; cache hits retain the same $0.20 rate. Cache writes and tools are billed separately. Pro, Max and Ultra memberships include Highspeed in Kimi web, Work and Code; API usage is billed separately. No independent Intelligence Index score has been verified for this speed variant, so it does not borrow the standard model score.
